subject: Business Models
title: SaaS-Enabled Marketplaces
description: Learn SaaS-Enabled Marketplaces in one minute.

hook.text: Shopify gives merchants tools to run their store. Then it connects them to buyers. Software first, market second.

buildup.text: SaaS-enabled marketplaces attract supply by offering useful tools before the marketplace even has buyers.

discovery.text: Mindbody offered booking software to yoga studios. Studios signed up for the tool—the marketplace came later.

twist.text: The SaaS locks vendors in. Once they depend on the software, activating the marketplace side is effortless.

climax.text: SaaS-enabled marketplaces solve the cold start problem by building one side before the other even exists.

punchline.text: Sell the tool first, marketplace later. Software is the Trojan horse.

quiz.question: How do SaaS-enabled marketplaces solve the cold start problem?
options: Attracting supply with useful software before building demand

details.summary: SaaS-enabled marketplaces provide software tools that supply-side participants need to run their businesses, using the tool as a Trojan horse to build a marketplace on top..
details.whyItMatters: SaaS-enabled marketplaces solve the cold-start problem by offering immediate standalone value through software tools..
takeaways: Software tools attract supply-side participants for standalone operational value
Once adopted, the tool aggregates inventory into a consumer-facing marketplace layer
This strategy solves the marketplace chicken-and-egg problem through tool utility

faq.question: How does a SaaS tool become a marketplace?
faq.answer: Step one: build software that supply-side businesses need regardless of the marketplace, like booking, inventory, or payment tools. Step two: once thousands of businesses use the tool, aggregate their offerings into a demand-side discovery platform..

faq.question: What are examples of successful SaaS-enabled marketplaces?
faq.answer: Mindbody provides fitness studio management software and aggregates class listings. Toast provides restaurant point-of-sale and enables online ordering. Shopify provides e-commerce tools and connects merchants with buyers through its marketplace..
